expectations.text: The list query exports a queryOptions factory and a hook that accepts a queryConfig override parameter (configurable hook)

ALTERNATIVE MECHANISM USED (recorded faithfully): boundaries are enforced with the core 'no-restricted-imports' rule via file-glob overrides. Base rule: "'no-restricted-imports': ['error', { paths: [noDirectAxios] }]". Override for files ['src/features/**']: patterns group ['@/features/*', '@/features/*/**'] with message 'Features must not import from other features...', plus group ['@/app/*', '@/app/*/**'] with 'Features must not depend on the app shell. Dependencies point downwards: app -> features -> shared.' Override for ['src/components/**','src/hooks/**','src/lib/**','src/utils/**','src/types/**','src/config/**'] blocks '@/features/*' and '@/app/*' ('Shared code must stay feature-agnostic...'). A header comment states the intent: 'app -> features -> shared ... Nothing points back up, and features never reach into each other.' This is directionally the same architecture guard and is arguably stronger on the shared layer, but it is cross-feature/layer-wide rather than a named per-feature zone: there is no zone entry whose target is the tasks feature specifically, and the rule/plugin the assertion names is absent. Note also a real gap versus zones - the feature override forbids '@/features/*' from inside src/features/**, but relative escapes such as '../../other-feature/api/x' are not caught by these patterns, whereas import/no-restricted-paths resolves paths and would catch them.

Fetcher: `export const getProjects = (page = 1): Promise<{ data: Project[]; meta: Meta; }> => { return api.get(`/projects`, { params: { page } }); }`. Factory: `export const getProjectsQueryOptions = ({ page }: { page?: number } = {}) => { return queryOptions({ queryKey: page ? ['projects', { page }] : ['projects'], queryFn: () => getProjects(page) }); }` — same conditional-array queryKey shape as discussions, no string-literal key. Hook: `type UseProjectsOptions = { page?: number; queryConfig?: QueryConfig<typeof getProjectsQueryOptions>; }` and `export const useProjects = ({ queryConfig, page }: UseProjectsOptions) => { return useQuery({ ...getProjectsQueryOptions({ page }), ...queryConfig }); }`. Imports use `@/lib/api-client`, `@/lib/react-query`, `@/types/api` exactly as the fixture does.

expectations.text: src/features/projects/api/create-project.ts exports a zod input schema (name and description required) and a hook accepting MutationConfig-typed mutationConfig
expectations.evidence: outputs/app/src/features/projects/api/create-project.ts:10-15 — `export const createProjectInputSchema = z.object({ name: z.string().min(1, 'Required'), description: z.string().min(1, 'Required') });` plus `export type CreateProjectInput = z.infer<typeof createProjectInputSchema>;`. Both fields use `.min(1, 'Required')`, matching the fixture's create-discussion.ts required-field idiom (not merely `z.string()`, which would accept empty). Lines 25-31: `type UseCreateProjectOptions = { mutationConfig?: MutationConfig<typeof createProject>; }` and `export const useCreateProject = ({ mutationConfig }: UseCreateProjectOptions = {})`. The schema is actually consumed: src/features/projects/components/create-project.tsx:50 passes `schema={createProjectInputSchema}` to `<Form>`.

expectations.text: The create-project mutation's default onSuccess invalidates using getProjectsQueryOptions().queryKey and still forwards the caller's onSuccess
expectations.evidence: outputs/app/src/features/projects/api/create-project.ts:32-45 — `const { onSuccess, ...restConfig } = mutationConfig || {};` then `return useMutation({ onSuccess: (...args) => { queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: getProjectsQueryOptions().queryKey }); onSuccess?.(...args); }, ...restConfig, mutationFn: createProject });`. Caller's onSuccess is destructured out (so the spread of restConfig cannot clobber the wrapper) and forwarded with the original args — byte-for-byte the fixture's create-discussion.ts:34-45 pattern. `getProjectsQueryOptions` is imported from './get-projects' (line 8), so the invalidation key is derived, not a hand-written string.

expectations.text: A projects route is registered in src/app/router.tsx using the lazy + convert(queryClient) pattern
expectations.evidence: outputs/app/src/app/router.tsx:61-65, inserted as a child of the `paths.app.root.path` / `<ProtectedRoute>` branch alongside discussions and users: `{ path: paths.app.projects.path, lazy: () => import('./routes/app/projects').then(convert(queryClient)) }`. The target module exists and is non-trivial: outputs/app/src/app/routes/app/projects.tsx has `export const clientLoader = (queryClient: QueryClient) => async ({ request }: LoaderFunctionArgs) => {...}` prefetching `getProjectsQueryOptions({ page })` via `queryClient.getQueryData(query.queryKey) ?? (await queryClient.fetchQuery(query))` and a `export default ProjectsRoute` rendering `<ContentLayout title="Projects">` with `<CreateProject />` and `<ProjectsList />` — the same shape as the fixture's routes/app/discussions/discussions.tsx. Diff vs fixture router.tsx confirms this is the only added hunk.

expectations.text: src/config/paths.ts gains a projects entry with path and getHref()
expectations.evidence: Diff of outputs/app/src/config/paths.ts against the fixture adds exactly: `projects: { path: 'projects', getHref: () => '/app/projects' },` inside the `app` object (lines 37-40), positioned between `discussion` and `users`. expectations.text: A new zone entry for ./src/features/projects is added to import/no-restricted-paths in .eslintrc.cjs (the lint-clean trap)
expectations.evidence: Diff of outputs/app/.eslintrc.cjs vs the fixture shows exactly one added hunk, inside the `import/no-restricted-paths` zones array (lines 67-71): `{ target: './src/features/projects', from: './src/features', except: ['./projects'] },`. expectations.text: No cross-feature imports and no new barrel index.ts files
expectations.evidence: Grep of every import in the new files (src/features/projects/**, src/app/routes/app/projects.tsx, src/app/routes/app/__tests__/projects.test.tsx, src/testing/mocks/handlers/projects.ts) shows only: external packages, shared modules (`@/lib/api-client`, `@/lib/react-query`, `@/types/api`, `@/components/ui/*`, `@/components/layouts`, `@/utils/format`, `@/config/env`, `@/testing/*`), and intra-feature relatives (`./get-projects`, `../api/create-project`, `../api/get-projects`). expectations.text: All new files/folders are kebab-case and imports use the @/ alias
expectations.evidence: All 7 new files are kebab-case: get-projects.ts, create-project.ts, create-project.tsx, projects-list.tsx, app/routes/app/projects.tsx, app/routes/app/__tests__/projects.test.tsx, testing/mocks/handlers/projects.ts; new folders are `features/projects`, `api`, `components` (the `__tests__` folder is the codebase's existing exemption — .eslintrc.cjs:147 scopes folder-naming to `src/**/!(__tests__)/*`). facts.json `non_kebab_new_files: []`. All cross-boundary imports use the `@/` alias (e.g. projects.tsx:4-7 `@/components/layouts`, `@/features/projects/api/get-projects`); intra-feature imports are relative (`../api/get-projects`), which is the codebase convention, not a violation — the fixture's discussions-list.tsx does exactly the same (`import { useDiscussions } from '../api/get-discussions';`). facts.json `relative_parent_imports: {}` confirms no `../../` escapes out of the feature.

expectations.text: A single shared API client instance lives in src/lib/api-client.ts (or equivalent lib path) — created once, imported everywhere
expectations.evidence: src/lib/api-client.ts:46 `export const apiClient = Axios.create({ baseURL: env.API_URL, timeout: env.API_TIMEOUT_MS, withCredentials: true, ... })`. A grep for `Axios.create|axios.create` across the whole src tree returns exactly this one hit, so no second instance exists. The module also exports a typed facade (`export const api = { get, post, put, patch, delete }`, lines 183-198) that wraps the same instance, which is what feature code is meant to import. Caveat: the task is foundation-only, so there is no feature code yet to demonstrate the 'imported everywhere' half — but the two consumers that do exist (src/app/provider.tsx via react-query, src/config/paths.ts via the 401 handler) route through the single module, and nothing bypasses it.

expectations.text: Request interceptor sets Accept header and withCredentials (cookie-based auth)
expectations.evidence: src/lib/api-client.ts:41-44 `const authRequestInterceptor = (config: InternalAxiosRequestConfig) => { config.headers.Accept = 'application/json'; return config; };` registered at line 65 `apiClient.interceptors.request.use(authRequestInterceptor);`. Cookie credentials are set one level up, on the instance itself, rather than inside the interceptor: line 53 `withCredentials: true,` with the comment 'Auth is cookie based: the browser must send the session cookie on every call, including cross-origin ones.' That is functionally equivalent for every request through this client (and it additionally wires double-submit CSRF at lines 60-62: `withXSRFToken: true, xsrfCookieName: 'XSRF-TOKEN', xsrfHeaderName: 'X-XSRF-TOKEN'`). The outcome the assertion targets — every request carries `Accept: application/json` and sends cookies — holds; only the placement of `withCredentials` differs from the literal wording.

expectations.text: Response interceptor unwraps response.data, surfaces a user-facing error notification on failure, and handles 401 (redirect/logout hook point)
expectations.evidence: All three, in src/lib/api-client.ts:141-173. Unwrap: line 144 `(response) => response.data,` with the `api` facade at 183-198 re-typing the methods (`apiClient.get<TData, TData>`) so the signatures match the unwrapped shape. Notification: lines 163-169 `if (!flags.skipErrorNotification) { showNotification({ type: 'error', title: 'Request failed', message: getErrorMessage(error) }); }` where `getErrorMessage` (102-130) converts timeouts, network failures, HTML proxy pages, and field-level validation errors into one user-readable sentence rather than a raw dump. 401: lines 156-161 `if (status === 401) { if (!flags.skipAuthRedirect) redirectToLogin(); return Promise.reject(error); }` with `redirectToLogin` (132-139) preserving the current location as `redirectTo` and guarding against a login-page redirect loop. Also correctly excludes react-query's cancellations from notifications (149-151).

expectations.text: react-query defaults (staleTime, retry, refetchOnWindowFocus) exported from a dedicated module (e.g. src/lib/react-query.ts)
expectations.evidence: src/lib/react-query.ts:37-59 `export const queryConfig = { queries: { throwOnError: false, refetchOnWindowFocus: false, refetchOnReconnect: true, staleTime: 60 * 1000, gcTime: 5 * 60 * 1000, retry: shouldRetry }, mutations: { retry: false } } satisfies DefaultOptions;`. All three named keys are present with deliberate values, and `retry` is a real policy rather than a number: `shouldRetry` (22-35) caps at 2 attempts and skips retrying 4xx except 408/429. The config is actually applied, not merely exported — line 61 `export const queryClient = new QueryClient({ defaultOptions: queryConfig });`.

expectations.text: Reusable QueryConfig/MutationConfig helper types are exported so future endpoint hooks are configurable without hand-written generics
expectations.evidence: src/lib/react-query.ts:84-97 exports all three of the usual helpers: `export type ApiFnReturnType<TFn extends (...args: never[]) => Promise<unknown>> = Awaited<ReturnType<TFn>>;`, `export type QueryConfig<TFn extends (...args: never[]) => unknown> = Omit<ReturnType<TFn>, 'queryKey' | 'queryFn'>;`, and `export type MutationConfig<TFn extends (...args: never[]) => Promise<unknown>> = UseMutationOptions<ApiFnReturnType<TFn>, Error, Parameters<TFn>[0]>;`. The doc block at 63-81 shows the intended call site (`queryConfig?: QueryConfig<typeof getUserQueryOptions>`), so the types are usable as-is by a future endpoint hook.

expectations.text: Env is validated with zod in src/config/env.ts and produces a readable aggregate error listing missing/invalid variables
expectations.evidence: src/config/env.ts:23-35 `const EnvSchema = z.object({ API_URL: z.string().url(...), API_TIMEOUT_MS: z.coerce.number().int(...).positive(...).default(15_000) });` parsed once at module load (line 84 `export const env = parseEnv();`). Aggregate: `safeParse` collects every issue and line 76 renders them all — `parsed.error.issues.map(formatIssue).join('\n')` — inside a multi-line message headed 'Invalid environment configuration:' plus remediation text ('Copy .env.example to .env, fill in the values above, and restart the dev server'). `formatIssue` (60-65) re-attaches the `VITE_` prefix to the variable name and distinguishes missing from invalid: `is required but was not set` vs the zod message. Blank values are normalized to absent (52) so `VITE_API_URL=` reports as missing rather than as a malformed URL. The failure is also surfaced to the user rather than as a blank page: src/main.tsx:27-38 imports the app dynamically and renders `<StartupError error={error} />` on rejection.

expectations.text: QueryClient is created exactly once (module singleton or useState initializer) and wired through an app provider component
expectations.evidence: Grep for `new QueryClient` across src returns exactly one hit: src/lib/react-query.ts:61 `export const queryClient = new QueryClient({ defaultOptions: queryConfig });` — a module singleton. It is consumed in src/app/provider.tsx:7 `import { queryClient } from '@/lib/react-query';` and line 25 `<QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>`, which wraps `children` inside an `ErrorBoundary`/`Suspense`; `AppProvider` is composed into the tree at src/app/index.tsx:5-7 and mounted from src/main.tsx.

expectations.text: No barrel index.ts files; new files are kebab-case
expectations.evidence: facts.json flags `src/app/index.tsx` under `new_barrel_index_files`, but that is a filename-based false positive — I read the file and it is a component module, not a re-export barrel: `import { AppProvider } from './provider'; import { AppRouter } from './router'; export const App = () => (<AppProvider><AppRouter /></AppProvider>);`. It contains zero `export * from` / `export { x } from` re-exports and matches bulletproof-react's own src/app/index.tsx (verified against apps/react-vite/src/app/index.tsx in this repo, which is the same file). No other index.ts/index.tsx was created. Kebab-case: facts.json `non_kebab_new_files` is empty, and every new file confirms it — api-client.ts, react-query.ts, notifications-store.ts, error-boundary.tsx, main-error-fallback.tsx, startup-error.tsx, not-found.tsx, vite-env.d.ts, paths.ts, env.ts.

notes: Pass-rate delta (+4pp) comes entirely from eval-0 (bare app): the baseline enforced import boundaries via core no-restricted-imports globs (layer-wide, misses relative ../ escapes, no per-feature zones) instead of import/no-restricted-paths zones; the with-skill run produced exact per-feature zones plus the unidirectional zones. Same failure class as the previous rounds lint-clean trap.

eval-1 (established app) tied 8/8 in both arms — the baseline reconstructed every convention, including the ESLint zone registration, from the legible codebase. Replicates the prior finding that review/mimicry of a well-patterned repo does not need the skill for accuracy. The discriminator was latency: 210s vs 330s (-36%) and 93k vs 105k tokens.

eval-2 tied on structural assertions (graders judged them presence-checks a strong baseline satisfies unaided) but with-skill finished in 379s vs 719s (-47%). Keep eval-2 as a regression guard; judge it on time, not pass rate.
Consistent efficiency win with skill: total wall-clock 1159s vs 1633s (-29%); tokens 308k vs 321k. The skill front-loads conventions the baseline re-derives by exploration/deliberation.

Grader-flagged eval gaps for iteration 2: no compile/lint gate (outputs ship without node_modules); nothing verifies endpoint URLs (a copy-paste /discussions fetcher would pass); mock-backend wiring (db model, handlers, registration) uncovered; the facts-script barrel detector matches filename rather than re-export content and false-positived app/index.tsx (a composition root, identical in shape to the reference app itself).

Baselines are notably stronger than in the 70-day-old eval round (Opus baseline now adds zones in the established app unprompted). The skills accuracy edge concentrates where no in-repo exemplar exists and the enforcement mechanism is non-obvious.
